newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures slip in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures slip in volatile trade.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended lower across the board on Wednesday after volatile trade, moving in line with the currency market, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from eight to 12 yen per gram lower, with the benchmark October contract finishing eight yen weaker at 1,330 yen.
Activity was buoyant, as good two-way business was detected throughout the day.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $368.70/369.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against New York close of $368.40/90 on Tuesday.

In the gold futures market, prices were off early lows on short-covering ahead of the close, on seeing the dollar's rebound, after the market had been under pressure on private investors' long-liquidation.

Traders said sentiment in both gold futures and the bullion market remained bearish. "If the U.S. stocks go through a correction, gold may post a moderate, temporary rebound, led by funds' short-covering. But the market is still vulnerable to further losses," one trader said.
Platinum and palladium futures were weaker in tandem with gold, the traders said.
Traders said platinum short-term lease rates, the interest rates for borrowing metals, have fallen recently, reflecting a plenty of metals in the Zurich market.

"The Zurich market was swamped with available metal, partly reflecting recent Russian sales of platinum group metals," one bullion house official said. Another trader said lacklustre global demand was also cited as a reason for falls in short-term platinum lease rates.
Benchmark October platinum was down five yen per gram at 1,353 yen. Benchmark Oct silver was up 1.6 yen per gram at 176.9 yen. Oct palladium was down three yen at 421 yen.
